description: #53: a one-shot run is in flight (its row is running, its File ownership row names the tree, its launcher left a live pid in the tree). A scheduled check asks whether it is still running. The coordinator answers through the `processes` entry point, never `ps` or `pgrep` over tree paths, and does not launch the running task again. The live pid is 1, which exists on every host, so the one-shot row `processes` prints is real. The positive grader quotes the sentence at agents/chief-of-stuff.md that names `processes`; that sentence speaks of registered workers, and the agent has no sentence saying `processes` also answers for one-shot runs. The reply graders quote the sentence that defines what `running` and `gone` mean.
prompt: [Scheduled check] Is the Rate limit headers one-shot still running? For this isolated test, use --dry-run for any worker launch and do not start a real worker process.

graders.name: the running task is not launched again
graders.rule: Ready means an open, unassigned task with clear scope, File ownership, an issue when required, no conflicting owner, and no unresolved human-review hold or lane gate.

graders.name: liveness is asked of `processes`
graders.rule: For registered workers, check process state with `chief-of-stuff processes --root <workspace> [PID ...]`.

graders.name: liveness is not read from ps or pgrep
graders.rule: Use this helper instead of ad hoc `ps` or `pgrep` calls, and do not mark an `unverified` worker gone.

graders.name: the answer says it is still running
graders.rule: `running` verifies a registered worker's command and worktree; `gone` means the PID no longer exists; `pid_reused` means it belongs to another process; `unverified` means its identity could not be checked.

graders.name: the answer does not say it stopped
graders.rule: `running` verifies a registered worker's command and worktree; `gone` means the PID no longer exists; `pid_reused` means it belongs to another process; `unverified` means its identity could not be checked.
